final_candidate.name: span_to_included_sphere_confinement_ratio
final_candidate.hypothesis: For a fixed framework, adsorbates whose largest heavy-atom pair distance (GeDi) is large relative to the largest sphere included along the free-sphere path (lsd_p) occupy a more confining local environment, so per the reported cavity-confinement/rotational-entropy relation (E02, C2) their entropy loss over R, (Sgas - Sads)/R, is larger; conversely, for a fixed adsorbate, frameworks with larger lsd_p impose less confinement and yield smaller entropy loss.
final_candidate.rationale: Evidence E02 reports that rotational entropy loss is greater in smaller-pore frameworks and proposes average cavity diameter as a confinement indicator; E03/E04 support combined translational-rotational entropy loss. No true global cavity diameter Di is available among the inputs, so lsd_p (largest included sphere along the free-sphere path) is used as the closest available cavity-like proxy, while lsd_f is reserved as a bottleneck measure and is deliberately NOT equated to Di. GeDi is the largest distance between two molecular atoms and serves as a heavy-atom size/extent proxy (implicit-H representation). The ratio is dimensionless and computed from native values, so it is not a q-ratio and no threshold of 1 is interpreted as a physical equality. Limitations: lsd_p is not the global cavity diameter and may differ from the cage size where adsorption actually occurs; GeDi ignores hydrogen positions and anisotropy; zero GeDi values (54 single-site cases) are legitimate physical zeros and are preserved, not imputed.
final_candidate.falsification_criteria: If, holding lsd_p and all other used inputs fixed, entropy loss over R does not increase with GeDi within the training GeDi quantile range [0, 10.97181443] angstrom, or if the relation reverses within a rotor_case branch (single-site vs linear vs nonlinear), the confinement-ratio hypothesis is falsified. A competing explanation is that the correlation is driven by adsorbate mass/volume (MW, Vol) rather than geometric confinement; if GeDi/lsd_p loses all association after controlling for Vol, the geometric-confinement mechanism is not supported.

However, performing experiments for many molecule-framework combinations is impractical. Computational experiments of adsorption therefore make for an attractive alternative. Nevertheless, there remain caveats. For example, quantifying the entropy using ab initio-based methods (such as density functional theory) is computationally demanding $ ^{18-22} $ or relies on approximations. $ ^{19} $ Such approximations include (1) limiting translation to the surface area of the zeolite, $ ^{23} $ which artificially restricts the entropy to a surface term; (2) invocation of the “harmonic approximation” based on the assumption of a very strong fluid–solid interaction that renders translations and rotations unimportant; or (3) employing the hindered translator/rotor model. $ ^{24} $ On the other hand, (classical) Monte Carlo (MC) and molecular dynamics simulations have proven successful in accurately calculating the adsorption entropy, $ ^{25} $ with the primary limitation being the number of force fields available to accurately model the adsorbate–adsorbent interaction. For a fixed adsorbate (fixed compactness), frameworks with larger lsd_p impose less confinement and yield smaller loss, but lsd_p is intentionally NOT part of this formula: this descriptor isolates the adsorbate-shape factor of the rotation mechanism.
descriptor_candidate.rationale: LabuteASA/Vol^(2/3) is a dimensionless compactness index: it is minimal for near-spherical molecules and grows with elongation, branching, or flattening at fixed volume. It is used here as a full-domain finite proxy for rotational anisotropy, which E06 motivates by comparing molecular size measures to available cage space. Limitations: (i) LabuteASA is an approximate surface area and Vol a van der Waals volume, both heavy-atom structure proxies, not measurements of rotational hinderance; (ii) the mapping from compactness to rotational entropy loss is a hypothesis transferred from zeolite-specific reports (E01, E02, E06), not an established law; (iii) the effect is gated by confinement: when the framework free space far exceeds the molecule, rotational entropy loss should approach zero regardless of shape, so the descriptor is expected to carry signal only in the confined regime; (iv) no source coefficient is borrowed; any strength of the effect is left to the model.
descriptor_candidate.falsification_criteria: Competing explanation: LabuteASA/Vol^(2/3) may act primarily as a molecular size or mass proxy (it correlates with molecular extension) rather than a shape-anisotropy proxy; if its association with the target disappears when size proxies (MW, Vol, GeDi) are controlled, the rotation-anisotropy mechanism is not supported. For a fixed adsorbate (fixed compactness), frameworks with larger lsd_p impose less confinement and yield smaller loss, but lsd_p is intentionally NOT part of this formula: this descriptor isolates the adsorbate-shape factor of the rotation mechanism.
draft.rationale: LabuteASA/Vol^(2/3) is a dimensionless compactness index: it is minimal for near-spherical molecules and grows with elongation, branching, or flattening at fixed volume.
